Subject: Registration link staggering + tracking approach for 'Build Faster: LLM Serving' webinar

Team —

Quick note as I finalize the invite sequence: we want to stagger registration links so each cohort (engineers, platform, architects, buyers) gets a unique link variant for attribution, but still land on a single canonical page to avoid SEO/dup issues. Proposed approach attached (segmentation_v3.csv) and draft copy attached (draft_invite_copy.docx).

Ask: can you review the tracking plan below and confirm we can generate the variants and short links by EOD?

- Variant mapping: cohort -> utm_campaign=llm_serving_q4, utm_content=engineer|platform|arch|buyer, source=redwood-email, hubspot_form=HS-49821
- Short links: bit.ly/redwood-llm-eng-<id> (we should reserve 6 per cohort for A/B subject tests)
- Calendar invites: please include the canonical calendar ICS and include the co-host CloudNative Labs in the event metadata

Attaching: segmentation_v3.csv, draft_invite_copy.docx, agenda_LLM_serving.pdf

Marissa
Marissa Cole | Sr. Field Marketing Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Registration link staggering + tracking approach for 'Build Faster: LLM Serving' webinar

Thanks Marissa — I like the single-canonical-page approach. A few notes from infra/SDK side: 

1) HubSpot forms: HS-49821 can accept a hidden field "cohort_variant" so we don't need separate forms for each cohort. That keeps reporting tidy.
2) Short links: we can create 24 short links and route them through our redirect service which appends a tracking hash for session-level analytics. That lets us measure first-page latency per cohort.
3) Cookie/consent: if we append hubspot query params we should ensure the canonical page reads them server-side and writes a cookie for later attribution (GDPR-friendly since it's first-party).

I put together a draft link mapping (attached as link_map_final.csv) — it contains the short-link, full URL + utm params, hubspot hidden field value, and expected landing behavior. I can generate the bit.ly entries once marketing confirms final utm_content values.

Two asks for today: 
- Marissa: confirm final cohort labels used in email copy (engineer/platform/architect/buyer) — these need to match the hidden field values exactly.
- Olga: can you push the canonical page to staging with the form hidden-field handling so we can QA links tomorrow?

If all good I'll loop in CloudNative to confirm they want distinct partner tags.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien | Partner Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
